## combat-only-fog

Blocks **9** cards.

- **(op)** a combat_only flag on the prevent_damage_permanent op, so a one-shot shield installed by a resolving spell on a targeted permanent (dealt 'by' or 'to', duration this_turn) prevents only combat damage and lets noncombat damage through
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: prevent_damage_permanent takes only objects, dealt and duration and prevents ALL damage, so it would also stop burn and fight damage; the prevent_damage static has combat_only but lives on a printed permanent, has no 'this turn' duration, cannot be installed by a spell, and only stops damage dealt to what it matches, never damage a creature would deal
- **(op)** a combat_only flag on the prevent_damage op (the player DamageShield), so a resolving instant installs a this_turn shield over every player (player: each/any) that prevents only combat damage and lets noncombat damage to players through
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: prevent_damage the op takes only player and duration and its DamageShield prevents ALL damage to the player, so burn and drain would also be stopped -- a strictly better card; the prevent_damage static has combat_only but lives on a printed permanent, matches only permanents via affects (no way to name a seat), and has no 'this turn' duration, so a spell cannot install it
- **(op)** a combat-only form of the one-shot player damage shield: `combat_only: true` on the `prevent_damage` op (and on structs.DamageShield, read by primitives.damage_player), so a spell can say "prevent all combat damage that would be dealt to players this turn" with player: "any" while noncombat damage to players still lands
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The `prevent_damage` op (op_options: duration, player) installs a DamageShield that prevents ALL damage to the player, noncombat included, so it would be a strictly better card; `combat_only` exists only on the `prevent_damage` static, which lives on a permanent's battlefield statics, matches permanents not players, and has no this-turn duration, so an instant cannot carry it
- **(op)** a combat_only flag on the prevent_damage op (the player DamageShield), so a resolving instant installs a this_turn shield over its controller (player: you) that prevents only combat damage and lets noncombat damage to that player through
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: prevent_damage the op takes only player and duration and its DamageShield prevents ALL damage to the player, so burn and drain would also be stopped -- a strictly better card; the prevent_damage static has combat_only but lives on a printed permanent, matches only permanents via affects (no way to name a seat), and has no 'this turn' duration, so a spell cannot install it. Populate itself is expressible (choose_permanents over creature tokens you control, then copy_permanent of the binding), so only the first sentence is blocked

  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `prevent_damage_permanent` takes only objects, dealt and duration and its shield stops all damage, combat and noncombat (a strictly better card); `combat_only` exists only on the `prevent_damage` static, which lives on a printed permanent and cannot be installed on a target by a resolving spell; the `grant_ability` op grants only triggered or activated abilities, not a static. - **(op)** a combat-only form of the prevent_damage op (e.g. combat_only: true on the op's player DamageShield), so a spell can say "prevent all combat damage that would be dealt to you this turn" without also shielding the player from noncombat damage
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The prevent_damage op takes only player and duration and prevents ALL damage to the player; combat_only exists only on the prevent_damage static, which is per-permanent, continuous while its source is on the battlefield and cannot name a seat, so neither fits a one-shot instant
- **(op)** a one-shot effect that prevents all combat damage that would be dealt to a player (you) for the rest of the current combat
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: the prevent_damage op takes only duration and player, with no combat_only narrowing and no 'this combat' duration; combat_only exists only on the prevent_damage static, which lasts while the permanent does rather than for one combat

That one leaf turns on every delirium card at once -- the printed clause is always "four or more card types among cards in your graveyard" -- and the same leaf reads "the number of card types among cards in your graveyard" on the effect side (Traverse the Ulvenwald, Emrakul's Evangel-style scaling), so it wants to land in `VALUE_KEYS` too.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `count` is the closest and is the wrong measurement: it counts *objects* matching a filter, so a graveyard of four creature cards reads 4 and satisfies a `>= 4` that delirium must reject, while a graveyard of one instant, one land, one artifact and one creature also reads 4 and passes by coincidence. That is the same distinction `values.py` already spells out for domain -- "five Forests are five and not one". `distinct` is the leaf that does count distinct values, but it is blocked twice over: its `DISTINCT_OF` allows only `power` (coven) and `basic_land_type` (domain), with no card-type entry, and it is absent from `STATIC_VALUE_KEYS` -- which is `{const, count, mana_symbols, counters_on, permanents_entered_this_turn}` plus the life and per-player leaves -- so even with a card-type entry it could not be named inside a static's `condition`. The `zone: graveyard` support in static counting filters that makes Threshold (Nimble Mongoose, `count` >= 7) and Hellbent expressible therefore reaches the graveyard but cannot ask what is in it. The remaining temptation is to enumerate: `any` of `all`-of-`exists` nodes over every 4-subset of the card types, which is 126 branches for nine types, silently wrong the moment a tenth type is printed, and an approximation rather than the sentence. ## impulse-from-opponent-library

Blocks **1** card.

- **(op)** a way to exile the top N cards of a *named* player's library and leave the impulse permission on the ability's controller rather than on that library's owner. Either a new key on look_at_top -- a 'playable_by' (or 'playable_controller') that makes _move_found write obj.playable_by = ctx.controller instead of the pid it looped over -- or, more generally, an 'as' binding on look_at_top recording the cards it moved (the way mill and exile already record theirs), so a following grant_playable can name them. Ragavan needs exactly one of these; with the binding, 'exile the top card of that player's library' becomes look_at_top {player: {binding: 'event_player'}, amount: 1, destination: 'exile', as: 'pilfered'} and 'until end of turn, you may cast that card' becomes grant_playable over {binding: 'pilfered'}
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: look_at_top is the only op that reaches the top of a library, and its playable_this_turn branch in effects/ops_cards.py _move_found hardcodes obj.playable_by = pid -- the player whose library was looked at. On Ragavan that library is the *opponent's*, so the printed 'you may cast that card' would grant the permission to the very player whose card was stolen: the opposite of the card. The exile op does set playable_by = ctx.controller, which is the right seat, but it takes a selector and selector_keys has no way to name the top of a library (no 'top'/'from_top' key; zone: 'library' with a count resolves to a chosen card from the whole deck, which is a tutor, not the top card). Composing the two also fails: look_at_top calls move_object without a 'by', so nothing records exiled_by and a follow-up grant_playable over {zone: 'exile', exiled_with: 'self'} matches nothing, while {zone: 'exile', player: ...} would match every card that player has ever had exiled. look_at_top has no 'as' binding either -- mill has one (Locke, Treasure Hunter) and exile has one, so this op is the odd one out. Naming 'that player' is NOT the gap: {"binding": "event_player"} already resolves to the damaged player, since primitives.damage_player fires COMBAT_DAMAGE_TO_PLAYER with player=pid.

## search-opponent-chooses

Blocks **1** card.

- **(decision)** a `chooser` on `search_library`/`search_zones` (a player spec, so it can be `{"target": ...}`) naming who picks from among the cards the search turned up -- the search itself is still performed and seen by the library's owner, but a *different*, targeted player makes the selection out of the revealed pool. Gifts Ungiven, Intuition and Plea for Power's kin all hang on it
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `_search` (src/commanderblitz/engine/effects/ops_cards.py) hardcodes the asker: it iterates `select_players(ctx, spec.get("player", "you"))` and passes that same `pid` into `ask_objects(ctx, prompt, pool, 0, take, pid, "search")`, so the searcher is always the chooser. The selector's `chooser` key exists (selectors.py, and it accepts an arbitrary player spec) but a search never routes its selector through `pick_from_pool` -- the selector is only a match test via `_matches_in_zone` -- so writing `chooser` on a search's selector is silently ignored and the caster would pick their own card, which is the entire card. `two_piles` (ops_cards.py) is the only op whose first decision belongs to somebody else, and its splitter is `ctx.opponents()[0]` rather than a target, it reads `library[:amount]` off the top instead of a searched pool, and the *controller* still decides which pile is taken -- the opposite of "target opponent chooses one".

<details><summary>Cards waiting on this</summary>

- **Intuition** (rank 1971) — `intuition`
  - Target opponent chooses one.
  - Put that card into your hand and the rest into your graveyard.

</details>

## search-split-destinations

Blocks **1** card.

- **(op)** a second destination on `search_library`/`search_zones` for the found-but-not-chosen cards (e.g. `destination: "hand"` plus `rest: "graveyard"`), so one search reveals N, a chosen subset goes one place and the remainder another, with the shuffle still happening once at the end
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `_search` resolves one `DESTINATIONS[spec.get("destination", "hand")]` and hands every picked card to `_move_found` (ops_cards.py); cards that were revealed and not taken simply stay in the library. `look_at_top` is the only lookup with a remainder key, `rest_to_bottom` (ops_cards.py), and it is a boolean hardwired to `_bottom_in_random_order` -- bottom of library, never the graveyard -- besides reading the top N rather than searching. `two_piles` does carry `to`/`other`, but only over the top of the library and only as a pile split. Sequencing two ops instead is an approximation, not the card: `search_library` to the graveyard followed by a `return_from_graveyard` would put all three cards through the graveyard, firing `leaves_graveyard` and inflating `cards_to_graveyard_this_turn` from 2 to 3, and `search_library` to hand followed by a `discard` would emit two `discard` events (madness, discard triggers) for cards the printing never discards.

</details>

## spells-cast-per-player

Blocks **1** card.

- **(value)** a value leaf that reports spells cast this turn *per player* rather than summed -- e.g. a `max_spells_cast_of: "each_opponent"`, or a per-player quantifier over a condition -- so "if **an opponent** cast three or more spells this turn" asks whether any single opponent reached three. Wanted by the whole Trap cycle and by storm-watching cards (Mindbreak Trap, Archmage Ascension-style counters, Guttersnipe-adjacent per-seat thresholds).
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `alternative_cost` with `{"mana": "{0}"}` and a `condition` is exactly the right home for this line -- that half is not the blocker. The condition itself is: `spells_cast_this_turn` (src/commanderblitz/engine/effects/values.py) resolves its player spec through `select_players` and then **sums** the ledger across every seat it names, so `{"spells_cast_this_turn": "each_opponent"}` is the *total* spells cast by all opponents. At a pod that is a strictly wider card than the printing: three opponents casting one spell each would switch on the free cast, which Mindbreak Trap does not do. The per-player machinery that exists, `max_count_of`/`min_count_of` via `_counts_per_player` (values.py), counts *objects* matching a selector one seat at a time and has no reach into the turn ledger's `spells_cast`; `condition_keys`' `any`/`all` combine sibling conditions and do not quantify over players.

<details><summary>Cards waiting on this</summary>

- **Mindbreak Trap** (rank 539) — `mindbreak_trap`
  - If an opponent cast three or more spells this turn, you may pay {0} rather than pay this spell's mana cost.
  - Exile any number of target spells.

</details>
